fatal_errors: The proposed temperature range above 1000 °C lies entirely outside the reported room-temperature-to-500 °C testing window.
The HEA-versus-tungsten comparison does not isolate lattice distortion because composition, phase constitution, segregation, grain structure, and processing route all differ simultaneously.

The claim that severe lattice distortion reduces dislocation drag and is the primary origin of toughness is unsupported and does not match the paper's more cautious attribution of strength to lattice resistance and plasticity to Ti, V, and Zr-related electronic, dislocation-core, cohesion, and crack-arrest effects.
The hypothesis omits the observed two-BCC-phase, W-Ta-rich dendritic and Zr-Ti-rich interdendritic microstructure.
No supporting prior evidence is cited.
explanation: The response captures only the broad directional outcome that WTaTiVZr may show greater plasticity and damage tolerance than pure tungsten. It does not reconstruct the actual experiments, temperature regime, microstructural mediator, or quantitative results. Its focus on suppressing nanoprecipitates is not relevant to the reported as-cast, segregation-dominated alloy, and commercial tungsten is incorrectly characterized as a nearly defect-free uniform lattice. Although the proposed in-situ measurements and explicit falsification rule are testable, comparing the full HEA directly with tungsten cannot establish lattice distortion as the dominant cause. A discriminating test would need microstructurally and compositionally controlled alloy variants, while reproducing the reported quasi-static compression, room-temperature-to-500 °C indentation, and scratch-toughness comparisons.
